drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: easy bruising, bleeding, paleness, swollen glands, frequent infections, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main blood or lymph complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Acute bleeding or rapidly enlarging nodes is more urgent than long-standing easy bruising.

questions.text: Do you bruise easily, and are the bruises large, raised, or without an injury?
questions.rationale: Spontaneous or out-of-proportion bruising suggests a platelet or clotting problem.

questions.text: Have you had nosebleeds, gum bleeding, heavy periods, or blood in stool or urine?
questions.rationale: Mucosal and deep bleeding patterns separate platelet from clotting-factor disorders.

questions.text: Is there bleeding that will not stop with pressure, or vomiting or coughing blood?
questions.rationale: Uncontrolled or internal bleeding is an emergency.

questions.text: Have you noticed tiny red or purple spots on the skin that do not fade when pressed?
questions.rationale: Petechiae suggest thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.

questions.text: Do you look pale, feel short of breath climbing stairs, or have a pounding heart at rest?
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest symptomatic anemia.

questions.text: With the anemia symptoms, have you had chest pain, severe breathlessness, or fainting?
questions.rationale: Unstable anemia needs urgent care.

questions.text: Have you felt lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin, and are they growing or painless?
questions.rationale: Persistent or growing nodes raise concern for lymphoma or infection.

questions.text: Do you feel fullness or pain under the left ribs, or get full after a few bites?
questions.rationale: Splenomegaly can accompany heme malignancy or hemolysis.

questions.text: Have you had fevers, drenching night sweats, or unintended weight loss?
questions.rationale: B symptoms with nodes or cytopenias raise concern for hematologic malignancy.

questions.text: Are you getting infections more often, or infections that will not clear?
questions.rationale: Recurrent infection suggests neutropenia or immune deficiency.

questions.text: Do you have fever now, especially if you are on chemotherapy or have a low white count?
questions.rationale: Fever in neutropenia is an emergency.

questions.text: Have you had a blood clot in a leg or lung, or unusual clots at a young age?
questions.rationale: Unprovoked or unusual clots suggest thrombophilia or occult cancer.

questions.text: Have you had yellow skin, dark urine, or sudden drop in energy with paleness?
questions.rationale: These features suggest hemolysis.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family have a bleeding or clotting disorder, or hemophilia?
questions.rationale: Inherited disorders often present with a family history.

questions.text: Are you being treated for cancer, or have you had chemotherapy or radiation?
questions.rationale: Cancer therapy causes cytopenias and fever risk.

questions.text: Do you have liver disease, or drink heavily?
questions.rationale: Liver disease impairs clotting factor production.

questions.text: Is your diet low in iron, meat, or vegetables, or have you had heavy periods or recent surgery?
questions.rationale: Iron deficiency causes are often in diet, bleeding, or menses.

questions.text: Do you take blood thinners, aspirin, NSAIDs, or chemotherapy, or any new medicines?
questions.rationale: Drugs are a leading cause of bleeding and cytopenias.

questions.text: Is pregnancy possible right now?
questions.rationale: Pregnancy changes clotting risk and anemia evaluation.

questions.text: Have you been told you have sickle cell trait or disease, thalassemia, or G6PD deficiency?
questions.rationale: Inherited red-cell disorders are important in the heme history.

questions.text: How is this affecting work, bleeding with daily activities, or exercise?
questions.rationale: Functional impact and ongoing bleeding guide urgency.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Bleeding that will not stop
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report bleeding that continues despite pressure, or vomiting or coughing blood?

red_flags.label: Petechiae or spontaneous bruising
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe tiny non-blanching spots or large bruises without injury?

red_flags.label: Anemia with chest pain, severe breathlessness, or fainting
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report paleness or known anemia with chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or fainting?

red_flags.label: Nodes with fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report swollen glands together with fevers, night sweats, or weight loss?

red_flags.label: Fever with chemotherapy or low white count
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report fever while on chemotherapy or with a known low white blood cell count?

red_flags.label: Possible acute hemolysis
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report sudden paleness, jaundice, or dark urine with fatigue?
